newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end off on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end off on profit-taking.

text.p: Profit-takers dragged Mexican stocks down from early record highs to end lower on Tuesday, traders and analysts said.
"There were stocks that had definitely yielded very good returns and so they stepped in to take profits," said Gerardo Copca, deputy research chief at the Valores Finamex brokerage.
The leading IPC share index ended down 7.74 points, or 0.20 percent, at 3,842.70. The IPC notched up an intraday record of 3,866.18 in early trade.
Volume was moderate at 91.8 million shares, but much improved on Monday, when U.S. markets were closed.
"The market was firm for most of the day. Profit-taking was absorbed very well, although some investors did get wet feet," a floor trader added.
Copca noted the bourse shrugged off record gains on Wall Street, where the Dow Jones closed up 1.12 percent at 7,067.46 points.

"The bourse did not react to the Dow rally, it reached resistance at 3,850 points after which investors were cautious. That may be a good thing, so the bourse can consolidate before gaining further," he added.
Traders said the bourse was generally firm due to forecast cuts in primary rates, although predictions were moderated during the day as the peso weakened.

A Reuters survey nN18546675 of nine money market traders in Mexico City showed they predicted an average assignment rate of 19.17 percent for bellwether 28-day Cetes rates, a fall of 52 basis points since last week.
This would be the lowest level for 28-day Cetes since the December 1994 peso devaluation crisis.
Banco de Mexico is due to release auction results at 1830 local time.
Traders noted profit-taking weighed most heavily on financial stock Bancomer and telecommunications stock Telmex, which together accounted for one-fifth of all shares traded.
Bancomer B shares ended off seven centavos at 3.26 pesos, while Telmex L shares fell 16 centavos to 15.48 pesos. Telmex ADRs meanwhile bucked the upward trend in New York to end off 1/8 at 40.
Holding company Femsa, one of the leaders behind Monday's record close on the bourse, was another heavily traded decliner, off 15 centavos at 28.35 pesos.
On the broad market, out of a total of 120 stocks traded, 54 ended up while 48 were down.

Mining and autoparts company San Luis was one of the most heavily traded top percentage gainers .PG.MX, up 1.80 pesos to 47.50 pesos on news its Rassini division was awarded a contract by General Motors, traders said. ((--Karina Balderas, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-9562))
